summary.vnce_server_role: The final C# Office Suite is the VNCE server.
summary.vnce_node_role: A remote laptop acts as a VNCE node/envoy.
summary.current_repo_state: CONTROL and SECURITY already contain VNCE lifecycle and attestation scaffolding, but SDK transport and remote trust remain mostly stubbed or local-only.
summary.overall_assessment: VNCE is conceptually shared across pillars, with CONTROL owning routing, SECURITY owning attestation/hardening, MAMA owning low-strain presentation, CORE wrapping envelopes, and SDK expected to supply adapter transport.

recommended_surgical_changes.change: Keep VNCE ingress CONTROL-owned and require SECURITY attestation before any remote display or input action becomes active.
Extend the AMIP contract for VNCE payload fields (protocol, workflow_lane, session_id, host, envoy_instance_id, device_identity, environment) while keeping the schema additive.
Create a formal internal AMIPI/VNCE dispatch schema so backend_ami, target_ami_id, mode, machine_profile, and correlation_id are standardized once CONTROL hands off internally.
Add remote-safe transport fields and trust tiers for LAN/internet because current SDK transport_policy and SECURITY trust posture are effectively local-only.
Implement SDK node adapters that can advertise frame/input caps, package VNCE envoy records, and send shunt-wrapped requests without taking routing authority away from CONTROL.
Use the updated Bucey Shunt lane and lock bits explicitly for VNCE handshake, resume, and approved session traffic.
Leave kernel-level work optional unless future latency or input-injection requirements justify real platform hooks; the current kernel folders do not yet carry VNCE logic.

risks_or_constraints: Current SECURITY trust posture treats only localhost/local_only/trusted_local as trusted, so LAN and internet VNCE will challenge or block without explicit expansion.
Current SDK shunt transport is local_only and stubbed; remote VNCE cannot be production-ready until transport is expanded.
CONTROL-only routing must be preserved; remote nodes must not call CORE, SECURITY, MAMA, or SDK directly.
STABLES token rotation and resume checks can challenge, quarantine, or require human verification if resume or token flows mismatch.
ADA and pacing constraints must remain active remotely: low-click, voice-first, reduced animations, and reduced cognitive load when needed.
The updated shunt map is more expressive than current runtime VNCE enforcement, so expansion must stay additive and not break existing local routes.
Kernel/reference-kernel folders do not currently provide live VNCE support, so relying on them now would create false confidence about low-level readiness.
